project.name: dedekind-ideal-arithmetic
project.description: Reusable ideal arithmetic, module indices and intrinsic heights of normed invertible modules over rings of integers. Ideal-norm comparisons, principal-prime extraction and class-group localization sit alongside finite section quotients, common scalar multiples, integral-section heights and normalized logarithmic heights, with tensor-product, positive metric-rescaling and equivalence-pullback formulas. Rational frames evaluate the same intrinsic height through coefficient-ideal norms and weighted archimedean products. Nonzero fractional-ideal norms factor as finite-support prime-norm products with signed exponents; over number fields, negative coefficient-ideal exponents give the finite-place numerator of height. Supplied frames extend to linear coordinates over semiring algebras. Over an infinite Dedekind domain with finite quotients, invertible modules have canonical definite ultrametric seminorms on their adic fibres, characterized in every rational frame by the residue cardinality raised to the signed coefficient-ideal count, times the coordinate norm. Principal fractional-ideal counts determine scalar adic valuations and residue-cardinality completion norms. Rank-one seminorm scalar extension, relative-degree formulas for weighted infinite-place products, fractional-ideal norm extension and isometric completion maps supply further interfaces.

review.notes: AI agents reviewed the ideal-norm, principal-prime and localization results; no human review is claimed.

methods.framework: AI agents using Lean and Lake
methods.tool_setup: AI agents composed Lean proofs using mathlib APIs and ordinary tactics such as rw, simp, constructor, congr, by_cases and typeclass inference. Toolchain and dependency revisions are pinned by the repository's Lean/Lake files.

automation.notes: AI agents authored the Lean proofs and documentation. AI involvement does not itself establish origin, correctness or rights.

scope: Ideal arithmetic, generic quotient indices, intrinsic fixed-field heights and their tensor, positive-rescaling and equivalence-pullback laws are described below. Supplied rational frames evaluate height through their coefficient-ideal norms and weighted rational-fibre norm products, or through residue-cardinality products with negative coefficient-ideal exponents and the same archimedean denominator. These products have finite support. Generic semiring-algebra coordinates of supplied frames and principal-count/completion-norm bridges also support canonical definite ultrametric seminorms on adic fibres of invertible modules over infinite Dedekind domains with finite quotients. The supplied-frame construction needs only a finitely generated module and a rational frame. The plus sign on its coefficient-ideal count does not change the existing height factors. Independently of norms and arithmetic finiteness, the valuation-integer span of integral sections is the image of the integer tensor fibre and spans the whole field fibre; it is finite for finite modules, and flatness gives an equivalence onto the span. The scalar right-unit model identifies the whole span with the valuation-integer ring. Generic fractional-ideal norm/index comparisons include zero ideals and sections; prime-exponent norm factorization requires a nonzero ideal, as supplied automatically by a rational frame. Weighted infinite-place products, fractional-ideal norm extension formulas, seminorm scalar extension and isometric completion maps supply further interfaces, not finite-extension-height evaluations. Element-norm witnesses, class-number computations, injectivity of class extension and proofs of proposed class generators are not supplied. The adic fibres are algebraic tensor products, not completed tensor products. Completed-lattice constructions, identification of seminorm unit balls with those lattices, local tensor compatibility and finite-extension height transport remain open.

highlights.title: Ideal norms, factorization and principal primes
highlights.statement: In an infinite commutative Dedekind domain with finite quotients, a nonzero smaller ideal has strictly larger absolute norm, and nested ideals of equal absolute norm coincide. Over a Dedekind domain finite free over the integers, each nonzero fractional-ideal norm is the finite-support product of height-one prime norms raised to signed integer exponents; the fraction field needs no number-field structure. In an infinite Dedekind domain finite free over the integers, a supplied element with prime absolute algebraic norm yields a principal prime above that rational prime. Over any Dedekind domain and fraction field, a nonzero fractional ideal contains a nonzero element whose principal ideal attains the same signed exponent at a fixed height-one prime; the ideal need not be principal.

highlights.title: Class groups under localization
highlights.statement: Class extension is surjective for torsion-free localizations of Dedekind domains, and a supplied class generator killed by extension makes the target a principal ideal ring and a unique factorization domain.

highlights.title: Section indices and rational-frame coordinates
highlights.statement: Nonzero sections of invertible modules over commutative domains with finite quotients span finite-index submodules; any two nonzero sections of one invertible module over a commutative domain admit a common nonzero scalar multiple. A supplied frame on K tensor_R M extends to an F-linear coordinate on F tensor_R M through compatible algebras over commutative semirings R and K, with F not required commutative, without finiteness or norm hypotheses. A finitely generated module with a supplied frame over a fraction field has a nonzero coefficient fractional ideal; torsion-freeness makes the coefficient map injective, but is not required to construct the ideal.

highlights.title: Intrinsic heights of normed invertible modules
highlights.statement: For a number field K, definite seminorms on the archimedean completion fibres of an invertible module over its ring of integers define a positive height equal to the section index divided by the weighted norm product for every nonzero integral section. Ordinary norms have weight one at real places and two at complex places. The normalized logarithmic height is (log index minus the weighted log norm sum) divided by [K:Q]. Tensor metrics multiply heights and add logarithmic heights. Positive placewise rescaling divides height by the weighted factor and subtracts its degree-normalized logarithm; equivalence pullback preserves both heights. Every rational frame evaluates this same height as the reciprocal of the product of its coefficient-ideal norm and the weighted archimedean product at its unit vector. Equivalently, the numerator is the finite-support product of residue cardinalities with negative coefficient-ideal exponents, with no extra finite-place weights. No integral basis is assumed, and only logarithmic height is divided by [K:Q].

highlights.title: Adic fibre seminorms and integral spans
highlights.statement: Let R be an infinite Dedekind domain with finite quotients, K its fraction field, p a height-one prime and F = p.adicCompletion K with its selected residue-cardinality norm. An invertible R-module M has a canonical definite ultrametric F-seminorm on F tensor_R M. For every rational frame e and every fibre vector x, its value is q raised to FractionalIdeal.count K p e.coefficientIdeal times the norm of e.fibreCoordinate F x, where q is the residue cardinality. The signed count appears with a plus sign, in contrast to the finite-place height factor. The seminorm is frame-independent and uniquely determined by this weight at the image of e.symm 1. On M = R the whole seminorm is the completion norm composed with the tensor right-unit equivalence; the same vector 1 tensor 1 has value one in every scalar frame. The supplied-frame constructor only needs a finitely generated module and a rational frame, not integral invertibility, freeness or torsion-freeness. No number-field structure, finite-free presentation over the integers, norm on K or norm or metric instance on a fibre is required. Over any Dedekind domain and fraction field, the valuation-integer span of integral sections is the image of the integer tensor fibre and spans the whole field fibre. It is finite for a finite module; flatness makes the image map an equivalence, and the scalar model identifies the whole span with the valuation-integer ring. These algebraic statements need no norm, infinite-ring or finite-quotient hypothesis.

headlines.title: Norm detects strict ideal inclusion and equality
headlines.text:
In an infinite
commutative Dedekind domain with finite quotients, `I < J` and `I ≠ ⊥`
imply `J.absNorm < I.absNorm`. If `I ≤ J` and the norms agree, `I = J`,
including zero ideals. No finite-free presentation over `ℤ` is needed.
See [strict comparison](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Ideal/AbsNorm.lean#L29)
and [equality](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Ideal/AbsNorm.lean#L42).

headlines.title: A supplied prime-norm element yields a principal prime
headlines.text:
In an infinite
Dedekind domain finite free over `ℤ`, a natural prime `p` and a supplied
`α` with `(Algebra.norm ℤ α).natAbs = p` give a principal prime above
`(p)`. This is conditional existence, not a search for `α`, a class-number
computation or a witness assertion for every prime. See
[principal-prime extraction](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Ideal/PrincipalPrime.lean#L27).

headlines.title: Localization can kill the class group and give a PID/UFD
headlines.text:
For Dedekind
domains `A, B` in possibly different universes, an `A`-algebra `B`
torsion-free over `A`, and
`IsLocalization M B`, extension `Cl(A) → Cl(B)` is
[surjective](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/ClassGroup/Localization.lean#L37).
If every source class is an integral power of a supplied `g` and `g`
extends to one, the library gives a
[PID](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/ClassGroup/Localization.lean#L59) and hence a
[UFD](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/ClassGroup/Localization.lean#L81).
Surjectivity needs no generator; neither class group need be finite.

headlines.title: Section indices and common multiples
headlines.text:
Over a domain, scaling a
nonzero section of a torsion-free module multiplies its quotient index by
the principal left-ideal index, including zero scalars and infinite quotients.
Invertible modules over commutative domains with finite quotients have finite
quotients by nonzero sections; over any commutative domain their nonzero
sections admit common nonzero scalar multiples. See
[module indices](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Module/Index.lean).

headlines.title: Intrinsic heights of normed invertible modules
headlines.text:
Over `𝓞 K` for a number
field `K`, definite seminorms on all archimedean fibres give a positive,
section-independent height: quotient index divided by the weighted norm
product. Invertibility, not integral freeness, is assumed. Tensor products,
positive rescaling and integral-equivalence pullback obey the expected
multiplicative and logarithmic laws. The normalized logarithmic height can
be negative. See [module heights](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/NumberField/ModuleHeight.lean)
and the [height guide](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/docs/RationalFrameHeight.md#intrinsic-height-and-sections).

headlines.title: Rational-frame and finite-place height formulas
headlines.text:
Every rational frame
evaluates this same intrinsic height as `1 / (N(I) * archimedeanProduct)`.
Nonzero fractional-ideal norms factor into prime norms with signed exponents
over Dedekind domains finite free over `ℤ`, without a number-field structure
on the fraction field. For number fields the height numerator uses residue
cardinalities with **negative** coefficient-ideal counts. See
[fractional norms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Ideal/FractionalNorm.lean) and
[finite-place height factors](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/NumberField/FinitePlaceHeight.lean).

headlines.title: Principal exponents determine scalar completion norms
headlines.text:
Over a Dedekind
domain and fraction field, a nonzero scalar has adic valuation equal to the
exponential of its negative principal-ideal count. For an infinite base with
finite quotients, its completion norm is the residue cardinality to that
negative count. No norm on bare `K` is chosen. See
[adic norms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Ideal/AdicNorm.lean).

headlines.title: Sharp signed fractional-ideal exponents
headlines.text:
At each fixed height-one prime
of any Dedekind domain, a nonzero fractional ideal contains a nonzero element
attaining its signed count. Together with Mathlib's `count_mono`, this is an
attained minimum. The witness may depend on the prime; no principality,
infinite-ring, finite-residue or `ℤ`-freeness hypothesis is needed. See
[count attainment](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Ideal/CountAttainment.lean).

headlines.title: Algebraic integral spans in adic fibres
headlines.text:
For any `R`-module `M` over a
Dedekind domain with fraction field `K` and height-one prime `p`, the span of
`1 ⊗ m` over the valuation integers in `F ⊗[R] M`,
`F = p.adicCompletion K`, is the image of
`O ⊗[R] M`, `O = p.adicCompletionIntegers K`. It is finite over `O` if
`M` is finite, and spans the whole fibre over `F`; flatness makes the image
map an equivalence onto the span. For `M = R`, the whole span corresponds
exactly to `O`. No finite-residue or infinite-ring hypothesis is used. See
[integral spans](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Module/AdicIntegralSpan.lean).

headlines.title: Canonical ultrametric seminorms on adic fibres
headlines.text:
For an infinite Dedekind
domain `R` with finite quotients, fraction field `K`, height-one prime `p`
and invertible `M`, the fibre `F ⊗[R] M` has a canonical definite
`F`-seminorm. In every rational frame, on every vector, it is the coordinate
norm times the residue cardinality raised to the signed coefficient-ideal
count, with a **plus** sign; negative counts are included. It is
frame-independent and characterized by its rational-unit-vector weight.
The supplied-frame constructor only needs finite `M` and a frame,
allowing torsion. For `M = R` the whole seminorm is the completion norm
pulled back along tensor right-unit equivalence. See
[adic seminorms](https://github.com/FormalFrontier/dedekind-ideal-arithmetic/blob/c76307595a1151abc42eacc9a815cb2d1bba6dc8/DedekindIdealArithmetic/Module/AdicSeminorm.lean).

main_results.name: FractionalIdeal.exists_mem_count_spanSingleton_eq
main_results.note: Over any Dedekind domain and fraction field, a nonzero fractional ideal has a nonzero member whose principal fractional ideal attains its signed exponent at a fixed height-one prime. The witness may depend on the prime; no principality, infinite-ring, finite-quotient or number-field hypothesis is required.

main_results.name: Module.adicIntegralSpan
main_results.note: For any module over a Dedekind domain and fraction field, the span over O = p.adicCompletionIntegers K of all sections in the algebraic adic fibre is the range of adicIntegralSpanMap. It is finite over O when M is finite over R, and its span over the completion field is the whole fibre. No norm or arithmetic-finiteness hypothesis is used.

main_results.name: Module.adicIntegralSpanEquiv
main_results.note: For a flat R-module M, the canonical map from O tensor_R M is an O-linear equivalence onto its integral span. Invertibility supplies flatness through Mathlib's projective-module instances.

main_results.name: Module.mem_adicIntegralSpan_self_iff
main_results.note: On every vector of the scalar fibre, membership in the integral span is exactly valuation-integrality of its coordinate under the tensor right-unit equivalence, not merely a statement at one pure tensor.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.adicSeminorm
main_results.note: For an infinite Dedekind domain R with finite quotients, fraction field K, height-one prime p and finitely generated R-module M with a supplied rational frame e, construct an F-seminorm on F tensor_R M, where F = p.adicCompletion K. It is definite, ultrametric and independent of the supplied frame. No integral invertibility, freeness or torsion-freeness of M, number-field structure on K or finite-free presentation over the integers is assumed.

main_results.name: Module.adicSeminorm
main_results.note: For Module.Invertible R M under the same ring and field hypotheses, this is the canonical adic fibre seminorm, without a supplied frame or additional metric data. It agrees with the supplied-frame construction in every rational frame. The construction uses A = WithAbs (NumberField.HeightOneSpectrum.adicAbv K p), proves NormedAlgebra A F using the norm-preserving algebra map, and reuses Seminorm.extendScalarsRankOne followed by F-linear base-change cancellation. No norm or metric instance is installed on K or a fibre.

main_results.name: Module.adicSeminorm_apply
main_results.note: For every rational frame e and every x in F tensor_R M, the value is (Ideal.absNorm p.asIdeal : ℝ) raised to FractionalIdeal.count K p e.coefficientIdeal, times the norm of e.fibreCoordinate F x. The count is signed and occurs with a plus sign. Pure-tensor, integral-section and rational-fibre evaluations are also provided; on the rational fibre the scalar factor is NumberField.HeightOneSpectrum.adicAbv K p (e x).

main_results.name: Module.adicSeminorm_unique
main_results.note: Among F-seminorms, the coefficient-ideal weight at the image of e.symm 1 uniquely determines the canonical seminorm. That image has value q raised to FractionalIdeal.count K p e.coefficientIdeal, where q is the residue cardinality.

main_results.name: Module.adicSeminorm_eq_zero_iff
main_results.note: The canonical seminorm vanishes exactly at the zero fibre vector. Definiteness is a conclusion of the construction, not extra data.

main_results.name: Module.adicSeminorm_add_le_max
main_results.note: On all adic fibre vectors x and y, N(x + y) is at most max(N(x), N(y)). As an F-seminorm it also satisfies N(a smul x) = norm(a) * N(x) for every a in F.

main_results.name: Module.adicSeminorm_self
main_results.note: On the scalar module M = R, the entire canonical seminorm is normSeminorm F F composed with the tensor right-unit equivalence, not merely an equality on integral pure tensors. The same integral vector 1 tensor 1 has value one in every rational frame; its coefficient-ideal weight cancels its coordinate norm.

main_results.name: IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_eq_exp_neg_count_spanSingleton
main_results.note: For any Dedekind domain R, fraction field K, height-one prime p and nonzero a, p.valuation K a is the exponential of the negative count of the principal fractional ideal generated by a. No finite-quotient or finite-free-over-integers assumption is required.

main_results.name: IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.norm_algebraMap_eq_zpow_neg_count_spanSingleton
main_results.note: With R infinite and having finite quotients, the norm of a nonzero scalar in p.adicCompletion K is the residue cardinality raised to its negative principal fractional-ideal count. The positive count weight therefore cancels the norm; no norm on K is chosen.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.scalarExtensionCoordinate
main_results.note: A supplied linear coordinate M equiv_R R extends to an F-linear coordinate on F tensor_R M over a semiring algebra. Its pure-tensor and inverse formulas hold without finiteness or norm hypotheses.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.fibreCoordinate
main_results.note: A frame on K tensor_R M induces an F-linear coordinate on F tensor_R M through compatible scalar towers over commutative semirings R and K and a semiring F. Pure-tensor, rational-fibre, inverse, frame-change and whole-equivalence unit formulas require no arithmetic, module finiteness, torsion-free, invertibility or norm hypotheses.

main_results.name: Ideal.absNorm_lt_absNorm_of_lt
main_results.note: In an infinite commutative Dedekind domain with finite quotients, strict inclusion with nonzero smaller ideal strictly reverses absolute norms. The nonzero hypothesis is not omitted.

main_results.name: Ideal.eq_of_le_of_absNorm_eq
main_results.note: Under the same ambient hypotheses, nested ideals with equal absolute norm are equal, including the zero-ideal case.

main_results.name: Ideal.exists_principal_prime_over_of_norm_natAbs_eq
main_results.note: In an infinite commutative Dedekind domain finite free over the integers, a supplied element with prime absolute algebraic norm yields a principal prime above that rational prime. The element and norm equality are hypotheses, not outputs.

main_results.name: ClassGroup.extendedHom_surjective_of_isLocalization
main_results.note: For Dedekind domains A and B with B an A-algebra torsion-free as an A-module and a localization at M, class extension is onto. No injectivity or finiteness of either class group is asserted.

main_results.name: ClassGroup.isPrincipalIdealRing_of_generator_of_isLocalization
main_results.note: With the same localization hypotheses, if every source class is an integral power of a supplied class g and g extends to one, then B is a principal ideal ring. Both generation and killing are inputs.

main_results.name: ClassGroup.uniqueFactorizationMonoid_of_generator_of_isLocalization
main_results.note: The same exact hypotheses imply unique factorization in B through the proved principal-ideal-ring criterion.

main_results.name: Submodule.cardQuot_map_of_injective
main_results.note: For an injective linear map f over a ring, the quotient index of p.map f equals p.cardQuot times the quotient index of the range of f, without assuming either quotient finite. For a nonzero section of a torsion-free module over a domain, scalar multiplication multiplies its index by the principal left-ideal index, including zero scalars and infinite quotients. Over an infinite commutative Dedekind domain, the scalar factor is the principal ideal's absolute norm.

main_results.name: Module.Invertible.finite_quotient_span_singleton
main_results.note: Over a commutative domain with finite quotients, the quotient of an invertible module by the span of any nonzero section is finite.

main_results.name: Module.Invertible.exists_nonzero_smul_eq
main_results.note: Any two nonzero sections of an invertible module over a commutative domain admit a common nonzero scalar multiple. No finite-quotient hypothesis or principal presentation is required.

main_results.name: Module.Invertible.cardQuot_span_singleton_tmul
main_results.note: Over a commutative Dedekind domain with finite quotients, for two invertible modules and nonzero sections m and n, the index of the span of m tensor n is the product of their section indices. The ring may be finite and the modules need not be free.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.height_eq
main_results.note: For a number field K and Module.Invertible (O_K) M, definite seminorms on all vectors of each completion fibre give a positive height equal to cardQuot (span {m}) divided by the weighted norm product for every nonzero integral m. Ordinary unsquared completion norms carry weight one at real places and two at complex places. No integral freeness or stored section-independence premise is assumed.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.normalizedLogHeight_eq
main_results.note: Under the same height hypotheses, the normalized logarithmic height at every nonzero integral section is (log index minus the weighted logarithmic norm sum) divided by [K:Q] and may be negative. The standard metric on O_K has multiplicative height one and normalized logarithmic height zero.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.height_tensor
main_results.note: For a number field K and invertible O_K-modules M and N with archimedean norms P and Q, (P.tensor Q).height = P.height * Q.height. The tensor metric is defined on every fibre vector and multiplies norms on arbitrary pure tensors of completion-fibre vectors under the canonical base-change comparison. No integral basis is assumed.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.normalizedLogHeight_tensor
main_results.note: Under the same tensor hypotheses, the normalized logarithmic height of P.tensor Q equals the sum of those of P and Q.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.height_rescale
main_results.note: For a number field K, an invertible O_K-module and positive factors c : InfinitePlace K → ℝ≥0ˣ, rescale multiplies each ordinary fibre norm by c_v. Its height is the original height divided by the product of c_v raised to InfinitePlace.mult v. The multiplicities are one at real places and two at complex places.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.normalizedLogHeight_rescale
main_results.note: Under the same rescaling hypotheses, normalized logarithmic height is the original value minus the sum of InfinitePlace.mult v times log c_v divided by [K:Q]. Height need not be at least one and logarithmic height need not be nonnegative.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.height_comap
main_results.note: For a number field K, invertible O_K-modules M and N, a metric Q on N and an equivalence e : M ≃ₗ[𝓞 K] N, (Q.comap e).height = Q.height. The source metric is the pullback on every completion fibre; no arbitrary metric change is permitted.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.normalizedLogHeight_comap
main_results.note: Under the same pullback hypotheses, normalized logarithmic height is preserved. Metric pullback itself needs neither module invertible and satisfies the identity and contravariant composition laws.

main_results.name: FractionalIdeal.absNorm_spanSingleton_eq_cardQuot_mul
main_results.note: For a Dedekind domain finite free over the integers and a fraction field, the principal fractional ideal generated by any element x of a fractional ideal I has norm cardQuot (span {x}) times norm I. Zero ideals and elements are included; infinite indices are zero. No number-field structure on the fraction field is required.

main_results.name: FractionalIdeal.absNorm_eq_finprod_count
main_results.note: For a Dedekind domain R finite free over the integers and a fraction field F, absNorm I equals the rational finite-support product of Ideal.absNorm p.asIdeal raised to FractionalIdeal.count F p I, over height-one primes p, provided I is nonzero. No NumberField F, Q-algebra structure on F or integral basis is required. At the zero ideal all counts vanish, giving product one rather than norm zero.

main_results.name: NumberField.FinitePlace.absNorm_eq_finprod_count
main_results.note: For a number field K and a nonzero fractional ideal I, the real cast of absNorm I is the finite-support product over finite places w of q_w raised to FractionalIdeal.count K w.maximalIdeal I, where q_w = Ideal.absNorm w.maximalIdeal.asIdeal is the residue cardinality. The signed exponents use no extra finite-place weights.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.height_eq_finitePlace
main_results.note: For a number field K, Module.Invertible (O_K) M, archimedean norms P and any rational frame e, P.height equals the finite-support product of residue cardinalities raised to the negatives of the counts of e.coefficientIdeal, divided by the product of P.rationalEval v (e.symm 1) raised to v.mult over infinite places v. Nonzeroness of the coefficient ideal follows from the frame. No integral section, integral basis, new height or further metric data are required. The denominator has weights one at real places and two at complex places; multiplicative height has no degree root.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.cardQuot_span_singleton_mul_absNorm_coefficientIdeal
main_results.note: A supplied rational frame for a finite torsion-free module over a Dedekind domain finite free over the integers gives, for every section, its span index times the coefficient-ideal norm equal to the principal fractional norm of its coefficient. No invertibility or freeness over the Dedekind domain is assumed.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.normProduct_eq_rationalFrame
main_results.note: In any supplied rational frame, the weighted norm product of every integral section equals the absolute field norm of its coefficient times the weighted rational norm product of the frame unit vector. This needs no finiteness, torsion-freeness or invertibility of the integral module and includes zero sections.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.height_eq_rationalFrame
main_results.note: For a number field and an invertible module over its ring of integers, every supplied rational frame evaluates the existing intrinsic height as the reciprocal of the product of the coefficient-ideal norm and the weighted archimedean norm product of its rational unit vector. No integral basis or second height definition is introduced.

main_results.name: NumberField.ArchimedeanNorms.normalizedLogHeight_eq_rationalFrame
main_results.note: Under the same height hypotheses, normalized logarithmic height is minus the logarithm of the coefficient-ideal norm and the weighted archimedean logarithmic sum, divided by [K:Q]. There is no degree root in multiplicative height and no nonnegativity assertion.

main_results.name: LinearEquiv.coefficientIdeal
main_results.note: For a commutative ring R, a fraction field F, a finitely generated R-module M and a supplied frame e : F ⊗[R] M ≃ₗ[F] F, the coefficient ideal is the nonzero fractional ideal whose elements are exactly e (1 tensor m) for m in M. The scalar module in its multiplication frame gives the unit ideal. Neither injectivity of M into its rational fibre nor integral freeness is assumed; this construction does not define a frame-independent height.

main_results.name: Seminorm.extendScalarsRankOne
main_results.note: For normed fields k and l with NormedAlgebra k l and an invertible k-vector space V, any seminorm p, possibly degenerate, extends uniquely to l tensor_k V with value norm(a) * p(x) on a tensor x. Restriction along 1 tensor x recovers p, definiteness is preserved when p is definite, and the unit line recovers the norm of l. No completeness or finite-extension hypothesis is imposed; this is not a height law.

main_results.name: NumberField.InfinitePlace.Completion.isometry_completionMap
main_results.note: For fields K and L with Algebra K L and infinite places v and w satisfying w.LiesOver v, Mathlib's completionMap extends the field algebra map and preserves the ordinary norm. The identity field map gives the identity on the completion. No number-field, finite-extension or real-place hypothesis is needed; no extension-height law is asserted.
